identity.title: Conjunctival rim pallor (and palmar crease / nail-bed pallor)

technique.how: In good light, gently pull down the lower eyelid and compare the colour of the anterior rim of the palpebral conjunctiva with the deeper posterior conjunctiva: pallor is present when the anterior rim is as pale as the posterior part, borderline when indeterminate. Also inspect palmar creases with the hand extended and the nail beds.
technique.prerequisites: Adequate lighting; examiner blinded to haemoglobin if possible.

interpretation.positive_finding: Definite conjunctival pallor roughly quadruples the odds of severe anaemia (Hb <=90 g/L, LR about 4.5) and warrants a haemoglobin measurement even without other clues.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of pallor only modestly lowers the probability of severe anaemia (LR about 0.6) and does not rule it out; it says nothing about acute haemorrhage before haemodilution.
interpretation.pitfalls: Agreement between examiners ranges from good with explicit criteria to near chance; conjunctivitis, icterus, dark skin and poor lighting mislead. Palmar-crease and nail-bed pallor add little.
interpretation.changes_what: Pallor present: check haemoglobin and look for a bleeding source; pallor absent: do not use to exclude anaemia or occult haemorrhage in a symptomatic patient.

estimates.population: 302 medical and surgical inpatients, tertiary-care university teaching hospital (prospective, blinded observers)
estimates.quote: LR 4.49 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.80, 10.99); pallor borderline, LR 1.80 (95% CI 1.18, 2.62); pallor absent, LR 0.61 (95% CI 0.44, 0.80)

estimates.target_condition: Anaemia, haemoglobin <9 g/dL (conjunctival pallor graded severe vs none)
estimates.population: 390 consecutive outpatient and medicine-inpatient adults >12 y, teaching hospital, rural India (prospective, blinded)
estimates.reference_standard: Haemoglobin by electronic cell counter within 1 day
estimates.location: Table 2 (PMC full text), conjunctiva rows; columns Hb <7, <9, <12 g/dL

estimates.target_condition: Severe anaemia, haemoglobin <7 g/dL (conjunctival pallor graded severe)
estimates.population: Same 390 patients, teaching hospital, rural India
estimates.reference_standard: Haemoglobin by electronic cell counter within 1 day
estimates.location: Table 2 (PMC full text), conjunctiva 'Severe' row, Hb <7 g/dL column

sources.citation: Sheth TN, Choudhry NK, Bowes M, Detsky AS. The relation of conjunctival pallor to the presence of anemia. J Gen Intern Med. 1997.
Kalantri A, Karambelkar M, Joshi R, Kalantri S, Jajoo U. Accuracy and reliability of pallor for detecting anaemia: a hospital-based diagnostic accuracy study. PLoS One. 2010.
Nardone DA, Roth KM, Mazur DJ, McAfee JH. Usefulness of physical examination in detecting the presence or absence of anemia. Arch Intern Med. 1990.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absence of pallor to exclude acute haemorrhage or anaemia in a patient with syncope, hypotension or chest pain - measure haemoglobin.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Pallor with tachycardia, hypotension or melaena = suspect haemorrhagic shock; obtain access, haemoglobin and cross-match immediately.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: With explicit rim criteria agreement was good: 'Kappa scores of interobserver agreement between paired observers were 0.75 and 0.54' (Sheth 1997, Abstract). Without them it was near chance: 'kappa values = 0.07 for conjunctival pallor' (Kalantri 2010, Abstract) and 'K scores ... ranged from .16 to .51 for other sites' (Nardone 1990, Abstract).

extraction_notes: Sheth 1997: LR for borderline pallor 1.80 (1.18-2.62) is in the quote but not entered as a field; sensitivity/specificity not in abstract; PMC full text retrieval failed (87 bytes). Kalantri 2010 Table 2 gives LRs by pallor grade (severe/moderate/mild/no) per Hb threshold; the lr_negative 0.38 for Hb <9 comes from the conjunctiva 'No' row, verbatim 'No  -  0.38 (0.19, 0.74)  0.40 (0.28, 0.58)' (Table 2), where the Hb <7 cell is '-' because no patient with Hb <7 lacked conjunctival pallor (text: 'absence of conjunctival pallor and tongue pallor completely ruled out the probability of haemoglobin <7 g/dL', Discussion) - entered as null rather than LR 0. Moderate-pallor LRs (2.32 at <7; 1.89 at <9) not entered. Prevalences from abstract: 'haemoglobin was <7 g/dL in 8% ... <9 g/dL in 21%'. Nardone 1990 reports no conjunctiva-only figures in the abstract; its composite values ('pallor at any one of three sites ... 0.65' sensitivity; 'pallor at conjunctivae, face, and palms (all three in combination; 0.95)' specificity; palmar creases specificity 1.00) are composites and were not entered as estimates. Nail-bed pallor was inferior to all other sites by ROC (Nardone, Abstract).
